transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I came because… honestly, it’s gotten hard to function at work. I keep hearing people talking about me, like through the conference room walls, or even from my phone when it’s off. It sounds like board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company.

And the strange thing is it’s so clear sometimes I’ll answer them out loud before I realize no one else heard anything. Which is embarrassing, obviously. I mean, I run meetings all day, I know what the acoustics are like in that building—actually, the conference room walls were redone last year and they still didn’t fix the echo—but this feels different. It’s just… I need help with that.
Do you ever see things that aren't there?

Seeing things? No, not really—at least that’s not the main thing. It’s more that I hear them. Like voices through the conference room walls, or coming from my phone even when it’s off, and it sounds like board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company.

And it’s so clear sometimes I answer back before I catch myself. Which is… you know, not ideal when you’re supposed to be the composed person in the room. The walls in that office have always been a problem, though—well, not always, but after the remodel they said the acoustics would improve, and they didn’t—but this feels different than just echo.
Do you believe what the voices are saying about you ruining the company is true?

I… I don’t know. Sometimes it feels true in the moment, because why would they keep saying it if there wasn’t something to it? But then I try to look at numbers, emails, the actual reports, and it gets all tangled.

The company has had problems—every company does, you know, especially with supply contracts and people missing deadlines, and last quarter the finance deck had three different versions floating around, which is ridiculous because I specifically asked for one source of truth. So when they say I’m ruining it, I can’t tell if it’s… like, a warning, or criticism, or just something I’m hearing.

I’m not sure what I believe all the time. It changes.
Do you find it hard to keep your thoughts straight or express them clearly when these voices are happening?

I’m not sure. I mean, people tell me I jump around sometimes, but I’ve always had a lot going on in my head—running a company, you have to keep ten threads at once. Emails, staff issues, contracts, who said what in which meeting…

When the voices are happening, I guess it’s harder to finish a thought, but I don’t know if that’s because of them or because I’m trying to listen and not listen at the same time. Like when someone’s talking during a presentation and you’re still expected to know the next slide. So… maybe? I don’t know how clear I sound right now, honestly.
Do these difficulties with keeping your thoughts straight happen only when you're hearing the voices, or at other times as well?

I’m not really sure how to separate it. I mean, thoughts don’t exactly line up neatly on a normal day either, but that could just be because there’s always something—emails, someone needing a decision, the calendar shifting, the legal team asking for a signature on something they should’ve finalized last week.

When the voices are there, it’s definitely… noisier, I guess. But other times I’ll still lose the thread, especially if I’m trying to explain something and I start thinking about the background of it, because the background matters, you know? People act like you can just answer one thing cleanly, but there’s always context.

So… maybe it happens outside of that too, but I don’t know how much is me being under pressure versus something else.
Do you think your thoughts are generally well-organized when you're not hearing any voices?

I mean… generally, I think so? But I don’t know what counts as “well-organized.” Like, if you asked my assistant, she’d probably say I make these lists that turn into three other lists, and then I remember something from a meeting two weeks ago that actually affects the first list, so it looks messy, but to me it’s connected.

When it’s quiet, when there aren’t interruptions, I can usually follow what I’m trying to do. But then I start thinking about the bigger picture—staffing, cash flow, the supplier issue, whether someone understood what I meant in an email—and then I’m not sure if that’s disorganized or just… how my brain works under pressure.

So I guess I haven’t really noticed it in a clean way. I don’t have a simple yes or no.
Do you think your thoughts are more disorganized when you're not hearing the voices and there's no immediate pressure or stress?

When there’s no pressure? I… honestly don’t know. That’s the part that’s hard to answer, because there’s almost always something going on, even if it doesn’t look urgent to someone else.

Like if I’m sitting alone with coffee, I might start with one thought—say, I need to pay a bill—and then I’m thinking about whether the accounting system is set up wrong, and then about the woman we hired who used to color-code everything, and how she said green tabs were “calming,” which I thought was strange but maybe she was right because the office did feel calmer then…

So is that disorganized? Or just thinking? I don’t really know. I haven’t paid attention to it in that clean, no-stress kind of situation.
Do you think your thoughts are typically disorganized even when you're not at work or dealing with any immediate issues?

I don’t know if I can say “typically.” When I’m not at work, I’m still… I don’t know, I’ll be making dinner or folding laundry and then I’m thinking about whether I answered someone too sharply, or whether I forgot to buy batteries, and then I remember this drawer at my mother’s house that always had batteries but never the right size, which used to drive me crazy because what’s the point of keeping them if—

Sorry. That’s kind of what I mean. I don’t always notice it as a problem unless someone points out that I didn’t answer the question. So… maybe sometimes, but I’m not sure if it’s disorganized or just my mind moving around.
Do you ever smell or taste things that aren't there?

Smell or taste? No, I don’t think so… not really. I mean, sometimes the office has that stale coffee smell even after the pot’s been washed, but that’s probably just the carpet or the vents, because that building holds onto everything.

The thing that brought me in isn’t smells, it’s more… hearing people. Like through the conference room walls, or sometimes from my phone even when I know it’s off. It’ll sound like board members, or staff, saying I’m ruining the company, and it’s so clear that I’ll answer them before I realize no one else heard anything.
Do you feel like your thoughts are jumbled or hard to follow when you're completely relaxed and not hearing any voices?

Completely relaxed is hard for me to pin down. I think… maybe? I don’t sit there and measure it, you know. If I’m relaxed, I might be watching something and then I’m thinking about the curtains needing to be cleaned, and then about this hotel I stayed in once where the curtains smelled like dust and oranges, which was odd—

Sorry. I don’t know if that means jumbled. I can usually follow myself, at least at first, but I lose the thread when I try to explain it out loud. So I’m not sure.
When you are alone, relaxed, and not hearing any voices, do you find it hard to keep your thoughts in order?

I’m not sure I can separate it that cleanly. Alone and relaxed… I mean, if the house is quiet, I’ll start thinking about one thing, like paying a bill, and then I’m thinking about the envelope, and then how paper cuts always happen in the worst place, and then this assistant I had years ago who used to open mail with a steak knife, which was ridiculous because—

Sorry. I don’t know if that’s “hard to keep in order.” It feels like I know where I’m going until I try to say it out loud, and then it sort of… branches off. So I haven’t really noticed it as a separate problem, if that makes sense.
Do you think your mind works in a similarly branching or tangential way even when you're a child or in your teenage years, before the current work pressures?

I don’t really know. I mean, as a kid I was always… I don’t know, busy in my head, I guess, but kids are like that, aren’t they? You think about homework and then the pencil sharpener and then the girl with the purple lunchbox, and it all seems connected at the time.

Teenage years are harder to remember clearly. I did okay when I had to, mostly. Or I think I did. I wasn’t sitting there wondering if my thoughts were organized, you know? Back then it felt normal because it was just my mind. I’m not sure how to compare it to now.
Did you have difficulty following your own thoughts or keeping them organized before you started hearing the voices?

I don’t know. Before the voices… it’s hard to slice it that way. I mean, I always had a lot going on in my head, but I didn’t think of it as “following my thoughts.” I just thought thoughts happened.

Sometimes I’d start with one thing and end up somewhere else, like thinking about work and then the carpet in an office and then how someone once spilled coffee in a meeting and everybody pretended not to notice— sorry, that’s not really what you asked.

I guess I can’t say for sure. I didn’t really notice it as a problem before, or I wasn’t paying attention to it that way.
Did you have difficulty keeping your thoughts organized before you started hearing voices?

I’m sorry, I know you asked that already. I just… I can’t really tell. Before the voices, I wasn’t measuring my thoughts like that. I’d go from one thing to another, sure, but it felt ordinary to me, like how you start looking for your keys and then remember the blue bowl by the door and then the apartment I had with the terrible hallway light—

So I don’t know if I had difficulty, exactly. I didn’t notice it as a problem then.
Did you consider yourself to have well-organized thoughts before you began hearing the voices?

Well-organized… I don’t know if I would’ve called them that. I wasn’t really thinking about my thoughts as organized or not organized back then. They just felt like mine.

I could do things, you know, make decisions, get through the day, but then I also remember my mind sort of jumping around—like I’d be thinking about a meeting and then the kind of pen someone used, and then this whole thing about stationery stores, which is not important. Sorry.

So… I’m not sure. I don’t think I had a clear idea of “well-organized” before all that.
Do you think your mind has always worked in a branching or tangential way, even before you started hearing the voices and experiencing work pressures?

I’m not sure. I mean, maybe? It’s hard for me to know what counts as branching versus just thinking.

I’ve always had a mind that goes places, I guess—like I’ll start with your question, and then I’m thinking about trees, because you said branching, and then the tree outside my old office that used to drop these little pods all over the sidewalk, and people would track them in on their shoes. Sorry, that’s not really the point.

Before all the work pressure, I don’t know that I noticed it as unusual. It just felt like how my mind worked. I can’t really say if it was always that way or if I’m only seeing it now because you’re asking.
Did you have any friends or family members comment on your thought process or how you explained things before you started hearing the voices?

I don’t really remember anyone saying it like that, like “your thought process is strange” or anything. My family would say I talk a lot sometimes, or I explain things the long way around, but families say that, don’t they? My sister used to roll her eyes when I’d start a story and then bring in five other people who weren’t actually in the story—because context matters, I always thought.

But before the voices… I don’t know. I can’t think of a specific time someone sat me down and commented on how I explained things. It’s possible they did and I brushed it off. I was busy, and people comment on all sorts of things, like tone or being too detailed or… sorry.

So, no, not that I can clearly remember.
Did your thought process change in any way around the time you started hearing the voices?

I don’t know if I can pin it down to “changed,” exactly. Around then everything felt… louder in my head, but not necessarily in the way I was thinking, if that makes sense.

I mean, I remember trying to answer emails and then noticing the subject lines were all kind of lined up wrong, visually—not wrong, just irritating—and then I’d think about the font, and who picked the font, and then how offices all use these bland fonts like everyone agreed to be boring. Sorry, that’s not what you asked.

So… maybe it got harder to stay with one thing? But I’m not sure if that was a change in my thought process or just me noticing it more because things were stressful and strange then. I can’t really say clearly.
Do you think the voices have made it harder for you to keep your thoughts straight?

Yes. I think they do. It’s like I’ll be trying to think through one thing, and then I hear them—through the conference room wall, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off—and it just takes over.

It sounds so clear, like board members or staff talking about me, saying I’m ruining the company. And then I’m not thinking about whatever I was trying to think about anymore, I’m listening, or I’m trying to figure out who said it, or I answer them before I even realize no one else heard anything.

So yes, it makes it harder to keep my thoughts straight. It sort of pulls the thread out of my hands.
Do you think your thoughts were as disorganized before the voices started as they are now?

I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think so, but it’s hard to compare because before all this I was busy all the time, and when you’re running meetings and jumping between emails and calls, everyone’s thoughts are a little scattered, aren’t they?

Like, I’ve always had a lot going on in my head. I’d be thinking about payroll, and then a client dinner, and then whether the lobby plants looked half-dead—which they did, by the way, and nobody ever watered them unless I said something. Sorry.

So… were they as disorganized before? I don’t think I can say that clearly. It feels worse now, but I’m not sure if that’s the voices or just me noticing it more.

patient.answer:
I don’t really remember anyone saying it like that, like “your thought process is strange” or anything. My family would say I talk a lot sometimes, or I explain things the long way around, but families say that, don’t they? My sister used to roll her eyes when I’d start a story and then bring in five other people who weren’t actually in the story—because context matters, I always thought.

But before the voices… I don’t know. I can’t think of a specific time someone sat me down and commented on how I explained things. It’s possible they did and I brushed it off. I was busy, and people comment on all sorts of things, like tone or being too detailed or… sorry.

So, no, not that I can clearly remember.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thought process was affected before the onset of voices
doctor.question: Did your thought process change in any way around the time you started hearing the voices?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about changes in thought process around the onset of voices, but the provided symptom profile does not include a specific item for disorganized thinking or thought-process changes.

patient.answer:
I don’t know if I can pin it down to “changed,” exactly. Around then everything felt… louder in my head, but not necessarily in the way I was thinking, if that makes sense.

I mean, I remember trying to answer emails and then noticing the subject lines were all kind of lined up wrong, visually—not wrong, just irritating—and then I’d think about the font, and who picked the font, and then how offices all use these bland fonts like everyone agreed to be boring. Sorry, that’s not what you asked.

So… maybe it got harder to stay with one thing? But I’m not sure if that was a change in my thought process or just me noticing it more because things were stressful and strange then. I can’t really say clearly.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thought process was affected by the voices
doctor.question: Do you think the voices have made it harder for you to keep your thoughts straight?

target_item.name: Hallucinations
target_item.manifestation: I came in because I keep hearing people talking about me through the conference room walls or from my phone even when it’s off, usually board members or staff saying I’m ruining the company, and it sounds so clear that I answer them before I realize no one else heard it.
target_item.reason: The question is directly asking about the voices, which are the patient's hallucinations, and whether they affect thinking.

patient.answer:
Yes. I think they do. It’s like I’ll be trying to think through one thing, and then I hear them—through the conference room wall, or sometimes from my phone even when it’s off—and it just takes over.

It sounds so clear, like board members or staff talking about me, saying I’m ruining the company. And then I’m not thinking about whatever I was trying to think about anymore, I’m listening, or I’m trying to figure out who said it, or I answer them before I even realize no one else heard anything.

So yes, it makes it harder to keep my thoughts straight. It sort of pulls the thread out of my hands.

doctor.intent: Determine if the patient's thought disorganization is a result of the voices or a pre-existing condition
doctor.question: Do you think your thoughts were as disorganized before the voices started as they are now?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about disorganized thought process before versus after the voices started, but the available profiles cover hallucinations, abnormal behavior, negative symptoms, impairment, and duration—not disorganized thinking or speech specifically.

patient.answer:
I don’t know. I mean, I don’t think so, but it’s hard to compare because before all this I was busy all the time, and when you’re running meetings and jumping between emails and calls, everyone’s thoughts are a little scattered, aren’t they?

Like, I’ve always had a lot going on in my head. I’d be thinking about payroll, and then a client dinner, and then whether the lobby plants looked half-dead—which they did, by the way, and nobody ever watered them unless I said something. Sorry.

So… were they as disorganized before? I don’t think I can say that clearly. It feels worse now, but I’m not sure if that’s the voices or just me noticing it more.

opening_question.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient's primary symptoms include hearing voices that are not there, which are a hallmark of psychotic symptoms. The voices are critical and comment on the patient's actions, which is consistent with a diagnosis of acute and transient psychotic disorder (F23). The patient's difficulty in keeping thoughts straight and organized, especially when hearing the voices, also supports this diagnosis.
